l3: My job is stuck in the running state and can't be stopped
description: An Automation job stays in Running state indefinitely and the standard Stop action does not terminate it. Covers force-termination via API/PowerShell and cancellation-request semantics. Excludes jobs that fail to start (see 'Job did not start as expected'), jobs that finished with Failed status (see 'Job Failed'), and Suspended state (see 'Job Suspended').

l3: My hybrid worker job isn't working properly
description: A job dispatched to an already-registered Hybrid Runbook Worker runs but produces incorrect behavior, wrong output, hangs without an error, or has unexpected side effects. Excludes installing/removing the Worker (see Hybrid Runbook Worker L2 leaves) and runbook startup failures on the Worker (see 'Runbook failed, or failed to start on Hybrid Runbook Worker').

l3: My runbook works locally but not in Automation
description: Same script succeeds when run locally (PowerShell/Python) but fails when uploaded as an Automation runbook — module/dependency differences, sandbox restrictions, identity differences between the local user and the Automation Account. Excludes Hybrid Worker behavior (see 'My hybrid worker job isn't working properly').

l3: Runbook to start or stop VMs
description: Guidance and patterns for runbooks that power Azure VMs on or off on a schedule or on demand — required permissions, scheduling, idempotent design. Excludes Update Manager maintenance windows and generic runbook errors.

l3: My runbook isn't working with managed identity
description: Runbook code that calls Connect-AzAccount -Identity (or equivalent) fails at execution time — token-acquisition errors inside a job, role-assignment gaps detected only at runtime. Excludes general Managed Identity configuration questions (see the Managed Identities L2 leaves).

One specific PowerShell cmdlet errors out — 'not recognized', missing parameter, or unexpected behavior — inside a runbook, typically due to module/version mismatches that mask the cmdlet. Excludes script-wide PowerShell errors (see 'Error running Powershell Runbook') and module import/update (see the Modules L2 leaves).

PowerShell runbook fails to execute or throws exceptions beyond a single missing cmdlet — script-level errors, parsing, permissions, runtime exceptions. Excludes a single-cmdlet failure (see 'Cmdlet not working') and Python runbooks.
Python 2/3 runbook fails to execute — import errors, syntax issues, runtime exceptions, sandbox limitations specific to Python. Excludes PowerShell runbook issues.

l3: Job did not start as expected
description: Job is queued or scheduled but never enters Running state — sandbox warm-up failures, schedule misfires, throttling. Excludes jobs that started then are stuck (see 'My job is stuck in the running state'), Failed jobs (see 'Job Failed'), and Suspended jobs (see 'Job Suspended').

Job entered Running state then terminated with Failed status — reading the Errors stream, classifying transient vs permanent failure, retry semantics. Excludes Suspended state (see 'Job Suspended'), stuck Running (see 'My job is stuck …'), and start failures (see 'Job did not start as expected').

Job ended in Suspended state because a checkpoint terminated execution (PowerShell Workflow) or an unhandled error caused suspension — resume semantics, checkpoint mechanics. Excludes Failed status (see 'Job Failed').

l3: I need help creating an Automation Account
description: Creating a new Automation Account via portal, ARM, Bicep, Terraform, or CLI — region/SKU selection, identity choice at creation time, linked Log Analytics workspace setup. Excludes existing-account migration (see 'I want to migrate to another subscription') and deletion.

l3: I am trying to delete or unlink an Automation Account
description: Cleanly deleting or unlinking an existing Automation Account — dependent resource cleanup (Run As accounts, Hybrid Workers, schedules), Diagnostic Settings, and common deletion errors (in-use, soft-delete). Excludes runbook/job deletion.

l3: I want to migrate to another subscription
description: Moving an Automation Account from one Azure subscription to another — move-resource flow, what does and does not move, schedule and link preservation. Excludes in-place upgrades within the same subscription.

l3: I need help with Source Control
description: Configuring Azure Automation Source Control integration with GitHub or Azure Repos for runbook sync — initial setup, sync errors, authentication, enabling/disabling sync. Excludes general runbook authoring and module management.

l3: I need help with Azure Automation Private Link
description: Setting up Private Endpoint for an Automation Account so jobs and webhooks reach the service over a private VNet — DNS, Hybrid Worker connectivity over Private Link, public access disabling. Excludes general networking issues unrelated to Private Link.

A DSC node reports non-compliance or failure when applying an assigned configuration — pull failures, LCM errors, partial-configuration issues. Excludes server-side compile problems (see 'Problem compiling a configuration') and template deployment (see 'My template did not deploy').

A DSC configuration template (.mof / .ps1) did not upload, did not deploy to nodes, or node registration to the Automation Account failed. Excludes the in-server compile step (see 'Problem compiling a configuration') and ARM template issues (see the ARM Template L2 leaves).

Compiling a DSC configuration in Azure Automation (Start-AzAutomationDscCompilationJob or portal Compile) fails — parameter mismatches, missing modules at compile time, partial configurations. Excludes runtime application of the resulting MOF (see 'Node configuration fails').

l3: Migrating Automation DSC to Guest Configuration
description: Plan and execute migration from Azure Automation State Configuration to Azure Policy Guest Configuration — feature parity, machine-by-machine cutover, timeline. Excludes only the DSC VM extension retirement (see 'DSC Extension Retirement').

Retirement of the DSC VM extension itself — deadlines, deprecation notices, end-of-life implications for VMs using the extension. Excludes the Automation DSC service migration (see 'Migrating Automation DSC to Guest Configuration').

l3: Installation or Removal of Hybrid Runbook Worker v1 (Agent based)
description: Installing or uninstalling the v1 agent-based Hybrid Runbook Worker on Windows/Linux machines — prerequisites, registration to the Automation Account, group join/leave, certificate handling. Excludes v2 extension-based (see 'v2 (Extension based)') and v1→v2 migration (see 'I need help migrating Agent-based to Extension-based Hybrid Worker').

l3: Installation or Removal of Hybrid Runbook Worker v2 (Extension based)
description: Installing or uninstalling the v2 extension-based Hybrid Runbook Worker via Azure VM extension or Arc machine extension — extension deployment, identity, removal. Excludes v1 agent-based and version migration.

l3: Runbook failed, or failed to start on Hybrid Runbook Worker
description: An existing Hybrid Runbook Worker is online and registered, but a dispatched job fails to start, errors immediately, or is rejected by the Worker host — Worker eligibility, network egress, sandbox issues. Excludes installing/removing the Worker and behavioral issues after a job has started (see 'My hybrid worker job isn't working properly').

l3: I need help migrating Agent-based to Extension-based Hybrid Worker
description: Step-by-step migration from v1 agent-based Hybrid Runbook Worker to v2 extension-based on the same machine — parallel running, group rename, validation, decommissioning v1. Excludes a net-new install of either version.
keywords: migrate hybrid worker v1 to v2
agent to extension hybrid worker migration

l2: I need help updating or importing a module
description: Importing PowerShell or Python modules into an Automation Account via portal, REST, or PowerShell — gallery imports, custom .zip packages, import errors. Excludes updating already-imported Az/AzureRM modules (see 'Update Azure modules').

l2: I need help updating or importing a module
description: Updating the bundled Az / AzureRM PowerShell modules in an Automation Account to a newer version — the built-in 'Update Azure modules' flow, version pinning, post-update breakage. Excludes importing brand-new modules.

l3: Getting errors when deploying an ARM Template
description: Concrete failures while deploying an ARM/Bicep template that creates or modifies Automation resources — quota, schema, RBAC, dependency errors. Excludes general guidance and best-practice questions (see 'Need help or have questions regarding ARM Template').

l3: Need help or have questions regarding ARM Template
description: Authoring guidance, parameter design, idempotency, and best-practice questions for ARM/Bicep templates that target Automation resources. Excludes specific deployment error troubleshooting (see 'Getting errors when deploying an ARM Template').

l2: I have queries related to Managed Identities based authentication
l3: I am facing unexpected errors while configuring Managed Identities
description: Errors during configuration of system-assigned or user-assigned Managed Identity on an Automation Account — role-assignment failures, identity association errors, propagation issues. Excludes runtime authentication failures inside a job (see 'My runbook isn't working with managed identity') and pure enable/disable workflow (see those leaves).

l2: I have queries related to Managed Identities based authentication
l3: I want details on system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities
description: Conceptual differences between system-assigned and user-assigned Managed Identity for Automation Accounts — lifecycle, sharing, role-assignment patterns, which to choose. Excludes step-by-step enable/disable and runtime errors.

l2: I have queries related to Managed Identities based authentication
l3: I want to disable Managed Identities from my Automation Account
description: Turning off (removing) system-assigned or user-assigned Managed Identity on an Automation Account — role-assignment cleanup and impact on running runbooks. Excludes enabling (see 'I want to enable …') and configuration errors (see 'I am facing unexpected errors …').

l2: I have queries related to Managed Identities based authentication
l3: I want to enable Managed Identities on my Automation Account
description: Turning on system-assigned or assigning a user-assigned Managed Identity to an Automation Account — role assignment to the new identity and converting runbooks from Run As. Excludes disable workflow and configuration errors.

l3: I need help creating Runtime environment
description: Creating a new Runtime environment in an Automation Account — selecting runtime (PowerShell 5.1, PowerShell 7.x, Python 3.x, etc.), default packages, visibility. Excludes linking runbooks to an existing environment (see 'I need help linking runbooks to Runtime environment') and ongoing management (see 'I need help managing Runtime environment').

l3: I need help linking runbooks to Runtime environment
description: Associating existing runbooks with a specific Runtime environment, switching a runbook between environments, and propagating that change to schedules and webhooks. Excludes creating the environment itself and managing its packages.

l3: I need help managing Runtime environment
description: Day-2 operations on an existing Runtime environment — adding/updating packages, version upgrades, retiring an environment, viewing usage. Excludes initial creation and runbook linking.

Onboarding and operating Azure Update Manager on Arc-enabled servers (on-prem / multi-cloud machines projected into Azure via Arc) — Arc agent prerequisites, hybrid registration to AUM, on-prem network requirements, Arc-specific licensing. Excludes generic Azure VM onboarding (see 'I need help to onboard to Azure Update Manager') and WSUS/Configuration Manager integration.

l3: I need help to onboard to Azure Update Manager
description: Initial onboarding of Azure VMs to Azure Update Manager — extension/AMA prerequisites, region availability, role assignments, verifying the first assessment. Excludes Arc-enabled servers onboarding (see 'Arc Enabled Servers') and integration with WSUS/SCCM.

Coexistence or replacement of on-prem WSUS / Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM/MECM) with Azure Update Manager — co-management modes, redirecting clients, deduplicating updates, retiring WSUS. Excludes Arc-only or Azure-VM-only onboarding (see the other 'Getting Started' leaves).

l3: Cannot add or remove from schedule
description: User cannot add a machine to a Maintenance Configuration schedule, or cannot remove one that is already attached — RBAC errors, machine eligibility, dynamic-vs-static scope conflicts. Excludes deleting the configuration itself (see 'Delete Configuration') and general schedule failures (see 'Schedule issues').

Deleting a Maintenance Configuration in Azure Update Manager — orphan handling, attached-machine cleanup, soft-delete behavior, errors when the configuration is in use. Excludes adding/removing individual machines (see 'Cannot add or remove from schedule').

Configuring and troubleshooting Dynamic Scopes (rules-based machine selection by subscription/RG/tag) for Maintenance Configurations — scope evaluation, tag matching, expected vs actual membership, scope updates not taking effect. Excludes static membership management (see 'Cannot add or remove from schedule').

A Maintenance Configuration schedule did not run at the expected time, ran on the wrong machines, or produced inconsistent run history — timezone, recurrence, missed windows, partial runs. Excludes Dynamic Scope membership problems (see 'Dynamic Scopes') and add/remove issues (see 'Cannot add or remove from schedule').

l3: I have questions about ARG query
description: Authoring Azure Resource Graph (ARG/Kusto) queries against Azure Update Manager tables for inventory, assessment, and history — syntax, schema, joins across tables, query performance. Excludes complaints about data accuracy (see 'Reporting inaccuracy').

Data shown in Azure Update Manager dashboards or ARG reports does not match what the machine actually has — stale assessment, missing machines, double-counted updates. Excludes ARG query authoring (see 'I have questions about ARG query').

Patch assessment on a machine returns Failed status — agent-side errors (AMA/MMA/Arc), update source unreachable, scan timeout, registry/WMI corruption. Excludes a successful assessment whose data looks wrong (see 'Reporting inaccuracy') and the actual install step (see 'Patching not started' / 'Update Failed or Not Installed').

How update classifications (Security, Critical, Other, Definition, etc.) are determined per OS and how to filter, target, or exclude by classification in deployments. Excludes Include/Exclude lists by KB ID (see 'Include or Exclude updates').

Configuring include/exclude lists (by KB ID, package name, or pattern) in a deployment schedule or one-time run, and troubleshooting why a listed update was or was not applied. Excludes classification-based filtering (see 'Classifications').

Server rebooted outside the configured maintenance window, or was expected to reboot but did not — reboot setting interpretation, dependency-required reboots, conflicting policies. Excludes reboot configured intentionally as a Pre/Post step (see 'Pre or Post').

A scheduled or on-demand patch run never began on the machine — orchestration did not reach the agent, machine offline at window start, prerequisites missing. Excludes patching that started but errored (see 'Update Failed or Not Installed') and the Assessment phase (see 'Assessment Failed').

Configuring or troubleshooting Pre-Task and Post-Task scripts (Azure Automation runbooks) attached to a Maintenance Configuration — invocation, output capture, failures, ordering relative to the patch step. Excludes general schedule issues (see 'Schedule issues').

Updates were installed that the user did not intend — wrong machine, wrong KB, outside expected scope. Covers Dynamic Scope drift, classification mis-targeting, policy overlap. Excludes failed installs (see 'Update Failed or Not Installed') and reboot issues (see 'My server rebooted unexpectedly').

Patch install on a machine returned Failed or NotInstalled state — installer exit codes, missing prerequisites, disk space, OS error logs (WindowsUpdate.log, dnf/yum log). Excludes the scheduling step (see 'Patching not started') and the Assessment phase (see 'Assessment Failed').

Azure Policy assignments specific to Azure Update Manager — built-in AUM policy initiatives (configure periodic assessment, schedule patches via Maintenance Configurations, etc.), DINE effects, exemptions, scope targeting. Excludes Machine Configuration policy compliance (see 'Machine Configuration > Policy Compliance > (General)') and the MC GuestConfiguration extension (see 'Machine Configuration > Policy extension problems > (General)').

OS or image is not supported by Azure Update Manager — supported version matrix, custom or hardened images, OEM/marketplace images lacking the required agent or update sources, end-of-support OS distros, requesting support for a new image. Excludes assessment failures on supported machines (see 'Assessment Failed') and onboarding flow questions (see 'I need help to onboard to Azure Update Manager').

Configuring update-related settings on machines managed by Azure Update Manager — patch orchestration mode (AutomaticByPlatform vs AutomaticByOS vs Manual), reboot setting (IfRequired/Never/Always), assessment mode (AutomaticByPlatform vs ImageDefault), and changing these at scale. Excludes maintenance schedules themselves (see Maintenance L2 leaves) and include/exclude lists in deployments (see 'Include or Exclude updates').

Configuring Azure Policy Guest Configuration on Arc-enabled servers — assigning policies, audit results, remediation, custom Guest Configuration packages on Arc machines. Excludes Update Manager classifications and policies (see Azure Update Manager L2 leaves) and the Automation DSC migration story (see 'Migrating Automation DSC to Guest Configuration').

l3: Cannot install the Connected Machine agent on Windows
description: azcmagent installer or PowerShell onboarding script fails on a Windows server — service install errors, MSI codes, MSI repair, prerequisite checks (PowerShell version, .NET, TLS). Excludes Linux installer issues (see 'Cannot install the Connected Machine agent on Linux'), removal (see 'Cannot remove my server from Azure Arc'), and upgrade (see 'Agent Upgrade').
keywords: install connected machine agent on windows

l3: Cannot remove my server from Azure Arc
description: User cannot disconnect or unregister an Arc-enabled server — azcmagent disconnect failures, leftover Azure resource, force-removal procedures, manual cleanup. Excludes the install path (see install leaves) and upgrade (see 'Agent Upgrade').
keywords: cannot remove server from azure arc

l3: Proxy server, private endpoint and other networking issues
description: Connectivity problems between azcmagent and Azure — proxy authentication, endpoint allow-list, Private Endpoint configuration for Arc, TLS interception, custom firewalls between server and Azure. Excludes pure installer failures (see install leaves) and AUM Private Link (see Update Manager Private Link leaf).

l3: Cannot install the Connected Machine agent on Linux
description: azcmagent install (deb / rpm / install_linux.sh) fails on Linux — package manager errors, dependency conflicts, SELinux blocks, distro or version not supported. Excludes Windows installer issues (see 'Cannot install the Connected Machine agent on Windows').
keywords: install connected machine agent on linux

description: Upgrading an already-installed Connected Machine agent (azcmagent) to a newer version — auto-update vs manual upgrade, rollback after a bad upgrade, blocked upgrade due to version skew. Excludes fresh install (see install leaves) and uninstall (see 'Cannot remove my server from Azure Arc').

Enrolling Arc-enabled Windows Server machines in the Hotpatching channel — eligibility (Windows Server 2022 Datacenter Azure Edition / supported SKUs), enrollment flow via portal or Azure Policy, license/subscription requirements, opting out, troubleshooting enrollment status. Excludes Update Manager patch settings (see 'Update Settings' under Azure Update Manager) and ESU enrollment (see 'Windows Server Extended Security Updates (ESU)').

The SQL Server extension for Arc-enabled servers — install/upgrade/uninstall, license type configuration (Paid/PAYG/LicenseOnly), inventory not populating, best-practices assessment failures. Excludes generic Arc agent issues (see Configuration and setup leaves) and other Arc extensions.

Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) extension on Arc-enabled servers — install/upgrade failures, Data Collection Rule (DCR) attachment, no logs flowing, transition from MMA. Excludes VM Insights stack (see 'Azure VM Insights') and other extensions.

VM Insights extension stack (Dependency Agent + AMA) on Arc-enabled servers — install, performance map, dependency view missing data. Excludes pure AMA without VM Insights (see 'Azure Monitor Agent(AMA)').

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) extension on Arc-enabled servers — onboarding, sensor health, removing MMA-based MDE, exclusion from Defender for Cloud auto-provisioning. Excludes Defender plan configuration inside Defender for Cloud itself.

l3: Problems with multiple extensions or other extensions not listed above
description: Issues that span multiple Arc extensions at once (conflicts, install ordering, shared agent failures), or single-extension problems for extensions not represented by their own leaf. Excludes any single extension that already has a dedicated leaf (SQL / AMA / VM Insights / MDE / Entra ID Login).

Entra ID Login extension (AADLoginForWindows / AADSSHLoginForLinux) on Arc-enabled servers — install failures, signing in to the machine with Entra ID, RBAC roles for SSH/RDP login via Entra ID. Excludes TPM-backed Entra ID usage (see 'Entra ID' under TPM L2).
keywords: arc machine entra id sign in

description: Creation of an AWS/GCP Multi-cloud connector or one of its solutions (Inventory, Arc Onboarding, Defender) fails — Azure RBAC, source-cloud credentials, connector resource provisioning errors. Excludes deletion (see 'Issues deleting resources or connector') and ongoing sync (see 'Issues syncing resources').
Deleting a Multi-cloud connector or its discovered resources fails — dependent solution removal, orphan handling, deletion stuck. Excludes creation (see 'Issues creating connector or solution').

After the Multi-cloud connector is created, automatic Arc-agent onboarding to discovered AWS/GCP instances fails — credentials propagation, SSM/run-command failures on the source cloud, instance ineligibility. Excludes connector creation (see 'Issues creating connector or solution').

l3: Issues related to authentication with AWS
description: AWS-side authentication problems used by the Multi-cloud connector — IAM role trust, missing IAM permissions, expired credentials, cross-account assume-role failures. Excludes GCP credentials and Azure-side identity problems.

Multi-cloud connector created and authenticated, but resource sync from the source cloud is delayed, partial, or shows stale state — sync intervals, scope filters, throttling. Excludes initial creation and Arc agent onboarding.

l2: Remote access to the server with SSH
description: Connecting to an Arc-enabled server over SSH using the Arc SSH proxy (az ssh arc / az connectedmachine connect) — required client extensions, Azure RBAC for SSH, port allowlist, hybrid-connection setup, troubleshooting SSH connection failures. Excludes RDP / Windows Admin Center access (see 'Remote access with Windows Admin Center') and the Entra ID Login extension for OS sign-in (see 'Entra ID Login extension issue').

l2: Remote access with Windows Admin Center
description: Connecting to an Arc-enabled server using Windows Admin Center (WAC) from the Azure portal — WAC extension install on the Arc machine, port 6516 / hybrid-connection setup, browser prerequisites, WAC sign-in failures. Excludes SSH access (see 'Remote access to the server with SSH') and the Entra ID Login extension (see 'Entra ID Login extension issue').

Enrolling Arc-enabled Windows Server (2012 / 2012 R2 and other end-of-support versions) in Extended Security Updates (ESU) via Azure Arc — license activation, billing scope, multi-year coverage, opt-out, license keys, and validating that a machine is receiving ESU patches. Excludes generic patch install issues (see 'Update Failed or Not Installed' under Azure Update Manager) and Hotpatching enrollment (see 'Enrollment in Windows Server Hotpatching').

Using TPM-backed credentials with Entra ID on Arc-enabled servers — TPM attestation for Entra device registration, key storage in TPM, hardware-bound primary refresh tokens. Excludes the Entra ID Login extension itself (see 'Entra ID Login extension issue').

Storing Arc Managed Identity credentials in the TPM — TPM-backed key protection for system-assigned MI on Arc machines, TPM hardware requirements, fallback behavior when TPM is unavailable. Excludes generic Managed Identity questions on Azure Automation (see those leaves) and the Entra ID Login extension.

l2: Issue viewing an Arc resource gateway
description: Issues viewing an Arc resource gateway in the Azure portal — gateway resource missing or not displayed, blade load failures, RBAC required to view, stale cache. Excludes creation (see 'Issues creating a new Arc Gateway resource') and deletion (see 'Issues deleting an Arc Gateway resource').

l2: Issues associating existing resources to a gateway
l3: Issues associating Azure Arc enabled servers to a gateway
description: Associating already-onboarded Azure Arc-enabled servers (Arc machines) to an Arc Gateway — gateway property update on the Arc machine, permission to mutate the resource, gateway scope and region match. Excludes associating Azure Local nodes (see 'Issues associating Azure Local to a gateway') and the gateway-resource lifecycle (see the create/delete/view leaves).

l2: Issues associating existing resources to a gateway
l3: Issues associating Azure Local to a gateway
description: Associating Azure Local (formerly Azure Stack HCI) clusters or nodes to an Arc Gateway — node-level gateway setting, prerequisites on the Local stack, region and Arc registration alignment. Excludes associating Arc-enabled servers (see sibling leaf) and creating the gateway resource itself.

l2: Issues connecting a resource through a gateway
l3: Issues connecting the Azure Arc enabled servers through a gateway
description: An Arc-enabled server is associated to an Arc Gateway but outbound traffic through the gateway fails — endpoint reachability via gateway, TLS, dual-stack fallback, gateway endpoint allowlist on the server side. Excludes the initial association step (see 'Issues associating Azure Arc enabled servers to a gateway') and Azure Local connectivity (see sibling leaf).
keywords: arc server traffic through gateway fail
arc machine outbound via gateway fail
arc gateway endpoint unreachable from server

l2: Issues connecting a resource through a gateway
l3: Issues connecting the Azure Local through a gateway
description: An Azure Local cluster is associated to an Arc Gateway but outbound traffic through the gateway fails — endpoint reachability, TLS interception, allowlist gaps specific to the Local stack. Excludes association issues (see 'Issues associating Azure Local to a gateway') and Arc-server-side connectivity (see sibling leaf).
keywords: azure local traffic through gateway fail
azure stack hci outbound via gateway fail
arc gateway endpoint unreachable from local

l2: Issues creating a new Arc Gateway resource
description: Creation of a new Arc Gateway resource fails — region/quota constraints, RBAC, ARM/portal flow errors, name collisions, missing prerequisites. Excludes association of resources to an already-created gateway (see the 'Issues associating' leaves) and viewing/deletion.

l2: Issues deleting an Arc Gateway resource
description: Deletion of an Arc Gateway resource fails or leaves orphans — gateway still referenced by associated Arc/Local resources, RBAC, force-delete procedure, soft-delete. Excludes disassociation of resources (handled under the 'Issues associating' leaves) and creation.
keywords: arc gateway resource in use cannot delete

description: Enabling Machine Configuration across many machines fails — Azure Policy assignment scope not converging, role propagation, DINE (DeployIfNotExists) effect issues, partial rollouts across subscriptions or management groups. Excludes single-machine enablement (see 'Enable a Single Machine') and remediation behavior on already-enabled machines (see the Remediation L2 leaves).

Enabling Machine Configuration on one specific machine fails — extension install on that VM/Arc machine, machine eligibility, system-assigned identity prerequisite, single-target Policy assignment. Excludes mass enablement (see 'Deployment at Scale') and remediation behavior on already-enabled machines (see the Remediation L2 leaves).

Continuous remediation mode in Machine Configuration — drift is auto-corrected on every evaluation cycle without user trigger; covers evaluation frequency, recurrence, and when continuous mode is the right choice. Excludes one-off remediation (see 'On-Demand') and turning remediation off entirely (see 'Disable').

Turning remediation off for a Machine Configuration assignment — switching from a Modify-style effect back to AuditOnly, removing remediation while keeping audit, impact on existing compliance state. Excludes uninstalling Machine Configuration itself (see Cannot Enable leaves) and the active remediation modes (see 'Continuous' and 'On-Demand').

Triggering a one-time remediation run on a Machine Configuration assignment — manual remediation tasks, ad-hoc target selection, when to prefer on-demand over the always-on continuous mode. Excludes the always-on flow (see 'Continuous') and turning remediation off (see 'Disable').

Migration topic from the Machine Configuration team's perspective — moving any prior configuration management (Automation DSC, DSC VM extension, third-party tooling) onto Azure Machine Configuration, including high-level migration patterns and choosing target effects. Excludes the Automation-side migration runbook (see 'Migrating Automation DSC to Guest Configuration' under Azure Automation) and the DSC VM extension retirement timeline (see 'DSC Extension Retirement').
keywords: onboard legacy config to machine configuration

description: Authoring a custom Machine Configuration package — DSC-based or Inspec-based authoring, GuestConfiguration PowerShell module, package signing, publishing to a Storage Account, testing locally before assignment. Excludes Microsoft-published baseline packages (see 'Baseline security issues') and enabling the assignment itself (see Cannot Enable L2 leaves).

Microsoft-published baseline Machine Configuration packages (Azure Security Baseline, CIS, STIG, etc.) — assigning baselines, interpreting compliance gaps, exemptions, drift after baseline updates. Excludes user-authored custom packages (see 'Authoring Custom Configuration') and general policy compliance reporting (see 'Policy Compliance').

Policy compliance reporting for Machine Configuration assignments — Compliance dashboard shows wrong state, machines reporting NonCompliant unexpectedly, exemptions, evaluation frequency. Excludes the remediation path that fixes non-compliance (see Remediation L2 leaves) and baseline-specific gaps (see 'Baseline security issues').

Issues with the Machine Configuration / Guest Configuration extension (AzurePolicyforWindows / AzurePolicyforLinux) on a target machine — install or upgrade failure of the extension, extension health, agent unable to fetch assignments, extension restart loops. Excludes generic Arc agent issues (see Arc 'Configuration and setup' leaves) and individual non-MC Arc extensions (see Arc 'Extensions' leaves).
